head: 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e

scope.reviewed: all 40 manifest files, read in full
scope.removed_reason: none removed; skill/hook/settings files kept in scope per ACTION-REVIEW-SEC-001

notes: Clean security lane: no new quantified exploit in cmd-ops. Known-ledger matches skipped: correctness-BLK-22-r1 (bootstrap settings.local.json overwrite), security-MIN-3-r2 (policy-guard path bypass), correctness-MAJ-24-r1 (acdsl ask rules removed), security-MAJ-4-r1 (additionalDirectories reconcile), correctness-MAJ-10-r2 (install.env unquoted). Cross-chunk suspicions for the station (not verifiable here): (1) cmd/bootstrap/run.sh passes auto-apply: decide unconditionally and BOOTSTRAP_EXTRA_PROMPT into a headless acceptEdits run on main; whether the unauthenticated loopback Welcome endpoint (internal/server/bootstrap.go) can be triggered cross-origin (CSRF) and which env it forwards decides whether this is a prompt-injection path — server chunk. (2) whether the auto-apply decide rules can apply smine-permissions allow-rule proposals, combined with the new casual orchestrate auto-merge + sync, is a skills-chunk question adjacent to security-MAJ-8-r1. Data-integrity observation (not security): .serena/ is now ignored as untracked by remove_agent_worktrees.sh/verdict.sh and treated as husk by worktree-sessionstart.sh sweep; Serena keeps project memories under .serena/memories, which these paths may delete.

walk.note: marker makes the routine opt-in — reduces unattended surface
orchestrate stage logs the same 300-char envelope excerpt as other stages; .orchestrate-report to stderr is agent prose

additionalDirectories grant-from-registry already known (security-MAJ-4-r1); orchestrate auto-merge is a casual-audience release decision (plan C7/C10, ACTION-REVIEW-SEC-005); launchd plist pins SMINE_AUTO_APPLY=never so the apply input remains user votes
OTEL endpoint becomes a per-install port marker; no secret in config
removed acdsl ask rules already known (correctness-MAJ-24-r1); new PreToolUse hooks only add denies; no allow-list widening in the diff
token prompt writes the token to the user's own file, never echoes it (unchanged); diff adds a shellcheck prereq only
winget install with consent prompt; no new surface

sources and rewrites install.env from the operator's own env (unquoted-write breakage already known as correctness-MAJ-10-r2); peek-port kill loop is limited to this user's listeners by lsof; no cross-principal input
default skill change; cell tool allowlist unchanged
test-only; sandboxed tmp dir with guarded cleanup
squash_contained uses read-only merge-tree plumbing; the deletion-safety predicate's soundness is a data-integrity concern, no attacker-controlled input
cache files under git-common-dir keyed by SHAs; read-only status tool, no exploit
untracked filter now ignores .serena/ and nested .DS_Store; operator-run tool, data-integrity not exploit
deny reason echoes the relative path and mode only
path-normalization / cwd-root bypasses already in known ledger (security-MIN-3-r2); hook is declared fail-open fast feedback, CheckPolicy is authoritative

subagent branch now ADDS requirements (spills of self-invoked skills) where it previously returned none — tightening; the skill name from the transcript only selects which existing file is required, no write or exec
deny reasons echo skill name / target path only
conduct gate for review lanes, documented fail-open; its context-read deny is bypassable via Grep/quoted cat, but it guards no confidentiality boundary — no exploit to quantify
.serena added to the husk allow-list for hollow, unregistered pool dirs; deletion scope is a data-integrity question, not an exploit (noted for station)
EOF now answers n — never prunes without explicit yes; safer
sources repo-local gitignored install.env; only install.sh / -install write it (no server writer: grep of internal/ and cmd/ at head), so it is operator-owned input
prints leaf counts and overlay path only
casual skillOverrides off/on flip touches only skillOverrides keys (merge, foreign keys preserved); repo-local settings re-enable is the documented design
OAuth token read from BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE into env only, never echoed; DRY output prints prompts, no token; results log keeps the same 300-char result excerpt shape as the nightly wrapper

settings.local.json overwrite already in known ledger (correctness-BLK-22-r1); the ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} results path is only symlink-attackable when TMPDIR is unset, which cannot be shown for the configserver-launched path from this chunk — no quantified exploit
__PEEK_HOME_ARGS__ is filled from the operator's own env/install.env by install.sh; no cross-principal input
install.env holds ports only; no secrets written or logged
writeInstallEnv writes integer ports and the split addr port; Run->RunSync is a timeout change; no exploit
new log lines print home paths and ports, no tokens or payload bodies

peekIdentity trusts a self-reported /healthz, so a co-resident user could spoof the homes; but the pre-change code reused ANY listener, so the guard is strictly tighter and introduces no new exposure; loopback gate unchanged
version bump of the pinned peek-mcp release URL only; no secret or payload logging added
unchecksummed release-asset download is pre-existing (jq line identical); diff only moves v1.2.0 -> v1.2.2, no new exploitable surface
adds install.env and .claude/settings.local.json ignores; keeps per-machine state out of commits
no exploit; ignore entries reduce accidental commit of local settings
version bump + build-install target; nothing logged
build-install runs ./install.sh, operator-invoked; no new trust boundary
